annotations.annotation_text: Page 193 opens Book 1, Chapter 7 ("Shem the Penman") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions, featuring Shem, Shaun (as Justius), ALP (Mercius). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 193 ("Shem the Penman"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shem" on page 193 ("Shem the Penman"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Shaun as Justius (193.31): Shaun assumes the persona of Roman justice, moral righteousness, and ecclesiastical authority, launching a venomous denunciation of his brother Shem.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp

annotations.annotation_text: The deathbone emblem (193.33): Shaun brandishes a bone / crucifix as an Australian aboriginal pointing-bone of ritual execution ('kurdaitcha'), threatening Shem with spiritual and bodily extinction.
sources: Frazer, Sir James George. The Golden Bough. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3623

annotations.annotation_text: The fratricidal indictment (193.35): Shaun accuses Shem of betraying Ireland, living in Parisian exile, forging counterfeit literature, and Wall Street financial ruin.
